name: RoG (Reasoning on Graphs)

paper.title: Reasoning on Graphs: Faithful and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning

construction.unit: KG triple (head, relation, tail) of an existing Freebase subgraph; relation-path knowledge tuned into the LLM
construction.kept_as: verbatim KG triples; which relation sequences exist is learned into LLaMA2-Chat-7B weights
construction.processing: offline only: shortest paths between question and answer entities of training questions give relation-path labels; one LLM is instruction-tuned on planning and on answering from retrieved paths
construction.writer: instruction tuning of LLaMA2-Chat-7B (3 epochs, 2 A100-80G, 38 h)

organization.structure: knowledge graph of entities and relations (Freebase subgraph; one subgraph per question in the released data)
organization.index: none beyond the graph: exact relation-name match starting from labelled question entities

management.operations: none; the KG is fixed and nothing is written at question time

retrieval.query: the fine-tuned LLM writes 3 relation paths for the question (beam search)
retrieval.candidates: breadth-first search from each labelled question entity that follows each relation path hop by hop
retrieval.selection: none: every complete matching path goes to the reasoner (shuffled and cut only if the prompt would exceed ~4k tokens)
retrieval.budget: K = 3 relation paths; no cap on reasoning paths; prompt limit 3,996 tokens in code

use.context: reasoning paths as 'e0 -> r1 -> e1 -> ...' lines, then the question
use.reasoning: single call to the same fine-tuned LLM returning all answers as a list; any other LLM can read the same paths

classify.note: The KG is given and never changed, so there is no management to place. The walk is planned by the fine-tuned LLM's relation paths, and the same LLM then picks answers from all matched paths; no score or top-k cut sits in between.

stages.ingestion: Questions arrive with their topic entities already linked to Freebase; the KG is a Freebase subgraph of triples within the maximum hop count of the question entities (2.57M entities, 8.31M triples).
stages.construction: Nothing is written at run time. Offline, the shortest paths between question and answer entities of WebQSP and CWQ training questions give relation-path labels, and LLaMA2-Chat-7B is instruction-tuned for 3 epochs to generate such paths and to answer from retrieved paths.
stages.organization: The KG stays a plain set of triples; the tuned model holds which relation sequences lead from question to answer.
stages.retrieval: The tuned LLM writes the top-3 relation paths by beam search; a breadth-first search from each question entity follows each path's relations in order and keeps every complete match.
stages.answer: All matched reasoning paths are written as 'entity -> relation -> entity' lines before the question, and the same LLM lists the answers; ChatGPT, Alpaca, LLaMA2-Chat or Flan-T5 can read the same paths instead.
stages.learning: Joint instruction tuning on planning (216,006 examples), retrieval-reasoning (30,465) and explanation data (2,000 answers written by ChatGPT).

summary: Treats a knowledge graph as the memory and teaches an LLM its relation vocabulary: the model writes relation paths as plans, the plans are executed on the KG, and the same model answers from the entity paths they retrieve.

headline: The memory is an existing KG and RoG writes nothing to it; what it learns is which relation sequences to follow, stored in the LLM's weights.
Retrieval starts from question entities the dataset already labels and matches relation names exactly; there is no embedding search.
Every path matching one of the 3 planned relation paths reaches the reasoner, so precision rests on the reasoning LLM (without it, WebQSP precision falls from 74.77 to 46.90).

paper_vs_code.code: a hit if any gold answer appears (normalised substring) anywhere in the whole generated answer list
all, unless the prompt would pass 3,996 tokens; then a random subset that fits

open_questions: RoG differs from the LLM baselines in fine-tuning as well as in retrieval; Table 16 (LLaMA2-Chat-7B fine-tuned without paths: 73.89 / 53.49 Hits@1) is the closer control than the zero-shot rows.
The non-LLM baselines are copied from UniKGQA and DECAF, so their answer extraction and Hits@1 definition may differ from RoG's substring-based scoring.

No run feeds the reasoner random paths of the same number, so how much of the gain is precise paths versus simply more KG text is not isolated (random plans retrieve different paths and also change their number).

discussion.takeaway: Use relation paths as plans: an LLM tuned to write paths that exist in the KG retrieves exact entity chains, and reading them lifts a 7B model above earlier KGQA systems on WebQSP and CWQ.

claims.claim: State of the art on KGQA.
claims.evidence: Hits@1 85.7 on WebQSP vs 82.1 for DECAF (+4.4%); 62.6 on CWQ vs 51.2 for UniKGQA (+22.3%), CWQ F1 56.2 vs 49.1. Table 1, §5.2.

claims.claim: Both planning and reasoning are needed.
claims.evidence: F1 without planning 49.69 / 33.76, without reasoning 49.56 / 22.26, random plans 35.24 / 37.64, vs 70.81 / 56.17 for RoG. Table 2.

claims.claim: The planning module plugs into other LLMs without retraining them.
claims.evidence: WebQSP Hits@1: ChatGPT 66.77 → 81.51, LLaMA2-Chat-7B 64.37 → 74.20, Flan-T5-xl 30.95 → 67.87. Table 3.

claims.claim: Generated relation paths are faithful: more of them cover more answers.
claims.evidence: Answer coverage of retrieved paths rises with K = 1…5 while reasoning F1 levels off; K = 3 chosen. Fig. 3, §5.4.

claims.claim: RoG transfers to another KG cheaply.
claims.evidence: MetaQA-3hop 88.98 Hits@1 after tuning from the Freebase model vs 84.81 from scratch; 2 h vs 38 h. Tables 12-13.

limits: The paper has no limitations section; it notes only that larger K brings more noise and retrieval time (§5.4, App. A.7.4) and that more Freebase QA data could help further (App. A.7.2).
reading: Question and answer entities are assumed labelled and linked to the KG (§3), so retrieval starts from gold entities; systems that must find entities themselves face a harder task.
The non-LLM baselines are copied from UniKGQA and DECAF (App. A.6) and the LLM baselines are zero-shot without KG access; fine-tuned LLMs without paths (Table 16) reach 73.89 / 53.49, closer to RoG.

The text reports Hits@1 gains of 8.5%, 15.3% and 119.3% for four LLMs, but Table 3 gives +22% for ChatGPT; in Table 3 the WebQSP cells of Alpaca + RoG (56.16 / 74.20) and LLaMA2 + RoG (74.20 / 56.16) look swapped.
RoG is tuned on WebQSP and CWQ together; trained on one dataset it scores 81.5 and 59.1 Hits@1 (Tables 14-15).
In the code the KG is an undirected simple graph, so a path can run against a relation's direction and parallel relations between two entities collapse to one.
Hits@1 in the code is a substring hit over the whole answer list, not the top-1 answer, which favours long answer lists.

abstract.text: RoG targets LLM question answering over knowledge graphs, where models lack current facts and invent reasoning steps. It plans with relation paths: a fine-tuned LLM writes sequences of KG relations that could lead from the question to the answer, the paths are executed on the KG to retrieve concrete entity chains, and the LLM reasons over those chains to answer and explain. The model is trained on two instruction tasks distilled from the KG, planning and reasoning over retrieved paths, and its planner can also feed other LLMs. It reports state-of-the-art results on WebQSP and CWQ with interpretable answers.
